# HAccordion

> Native details/summary disclosures with single or multiple expansion.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.5.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HAccordion` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-accordion>`.
- Constructor: `HearthAccordionElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HAccordion.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- The model is always an array of open IDs, including in single-expansion mode. Set multiple to allow several sections.
- Native details/summary provides disclosure behavior and keyboard activation. A slot named by item.id overrides its description fallback.
- Do not replace disclosure semantics with tab roles.

## Public API

items: {id, title, description?, disabled?}[] · modelValue, value: string[] · multiple: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: AccordionItem[];
    modelValue?: string[];
    value?: string[];
    multiple?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [], value: () => [] }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(ids), change(ids)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        value: string[]
    ];
    change: [
        value: string[]
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

One named slot per item.id

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, item, trigger, panel

Use `hearth-accordion::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface AccordionItem {
    id: string;
    title: string;
    description?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { HAccordion } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const open = ref<string[]>([]);
const items = [{ id: 'storage', title: 'Where is data stored?' }];
</script>

<template>
  <HAccordion v-model="open" :items="items">
    <template #storage>Your application owns its storage.</template>
  </HAccordion>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-accordion');
Object.assign(element, {
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "storage",
      "title": "Where is data stored?"
    }
  ]
});

element.innerHTML = "<div slot=\"storage\">Your application owns its storage.</div>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
